title: Amount Disbursed under Self-employed Relief Scheme and Further Measures to Help Self-employed
what_it_is: Amount Disbursed under Self-employed Relief Scheme and Further Measures to Help Self-employed

sections.label: Self-employed Relief Scheme questions
sections.summary: Questions asked on SIRS disbursement, future allocations and reasons for rejected appeals, with eligible SEPs receiving three $3,000 tranches in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the current amount disbursed under the Self-employed Relief Scheme as compared to its budgetary allocation; (b) whether there are plans for more allocations should the economic outlook remain bleak beyond the next one year; and (c) what are the various reasons for the rejection of appeals under this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Eligible SEPs receive three tranches of $3,000 each in May, July and October 2020.

sections.label: SIRS disbursement and applications
sections.summary: Over $1.1 billion disbursed in two tranches; SIRS expected to cost $2 billion, with about 190,000 recipients and two in three applications approved.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over $1.1 billion has been disbursed in the first two tranches.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With the third and final tranche, SIRS is expected to cost $2 billion in total, almost double the original $1.2 billion set aside.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Altogether, about 190,000 individuals have received SIRS, with about 100,000 qualifying automatically, and 90,000 through application.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: About two in three applications have been approved.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the remaining one-third, applicants may have been earning much higher incomes, residing in high value properties or own two or more property with their spouses.

sections.label: Support beyond existing schemes
sections.summary: Government is studying ways to support vulnerable employees and SEPs beyond existing schemes, as announced by Heng Swee Keat on 17 August 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat in his Ministerial Statement on 17 August 2020, the Government is studying appropriate ways to support employees and SEPs who are most vulnerable, beyond the existing schemes.
